nodes.description: Rspo2 is expressed in the apical ectodermal ridge (AER) of all limb buds. In Rspo2-null mice the AER is induced normally, but expression of AER markers (Fgf8, Fgf4) and of beta-catenin targets within the AER is not maintained, and Shh signalling in the limb is reduced. Without a maintained AER the limb bud cannot grow out; in mice the defect is most severe distally and in the hindlimb, whereas human null alleles abolish all four limbs.

nodes.description: R-spondin 2 signalling through the canonical WNT pathway is needed for branching of the developing lung. Hypomorphic Rspo2 mice have hypoplastic lungs with reduced branching and reduced WNT reporter activity, and further loss of WNT co-receptor function (Lrp6) makes the hypoplasia more severe. In humans with RSPO2 null alleles the lungs fail to form.

nodes.description: RSPO2 acts as a direct antagonistic ligand of the transmembrane E3 ligases RNF43 and ZNRF3. Without it, these ligases remain active and WNT/beta-catenin signalling in responsive tissues is not amplified. The limb-relevant activity does not require the LGR4/5/6 receptors: a ubiquitous triple Lgr4/5/6 knockout mouse does not reproduce the Rspo2 loss-of-function phenotype, whereas concurrent loss of rnf43 and znrf3 in Xenopus produces supernumerary limbs, the mirror image of amelia.

evidence.reference_title: RSPO2 inhibition of RNF43 and ZNRF3 governs limb development independently of LGR4/5/6.
evidence.snippet: Our results establish that RSPO2, without the LGR4/5/6 receptors, serves as a direct antagonistic ligand to RNF43 and ZNRF3, which together constitute a master switch that governs limb specification.

evidence.snippet: Instead, we found that the concurrent deletion of rnf43 and znrf3 in Xenopus embryos was sufficient to trigger the outgrowth of supernumerary limbs.
